title: E2E latency spike: streamed-audio fixture through eaRS STT blocks on turn_interrupted loops
description:
Goal: measure end-to-end first-audio (baseline vs voice-cascade) with a real streamed utterance: spgx/spqx-generated question WAV -> gateway -> STT -> brain -> TTS, reading trace events (brain_first_token, tts_audio_start, frontend_audio_play_scheduled). Parent epic fxl-xwd9.

Assembled so far (all reusable):
- /tmp/spike-question.wav — "What's the tallest mountain in the world, and who first climbed it?" synthesized via spqx say with mei_ling canned reference (ad-hoc cloning; spqx config points model.id at cached Base-4bit since Base-6bit isn't in HF cache).
- agents/spike-campbell/ workspace: campbell copy + .foxline/loadout.toml (model mac-gemma/gemma-4-26b-a4b because LM Studio :1234 is down; tools + ask_orchestrator; extensions=["local:voice-cascade"]) + extension copied into .foxline/extensions/.
- Two spike gateways built and run: :8781 FOXLINE_CASCADE=1, :8782 =0, config /tmp/foxline-{spike,base}.toml (trace_dir per run), env FOXLINE_TTS_MODEL_PATH=<cached 4bit snapshot>, FOXLINE_STT_BACKEND=ears, FOXLINE_STT_WS_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:8798/ws.
- Fixture invocation pattern: bun benchmarks/run-rust-gateway-fixture.ts --url=ws://... --agent=campbell --workspace=agents/spike-campbell --audio-file=/tmp/spike-question.wav ... (NOTE: fixture args need `--key=value` form; space-separated silently falls back to defaults).

Blockers found (pre-existing, this spike is blocked on them):
1. parakeet-cpp-stt-worker binary missing from ~/repos/pibot/native/parakeet-cpp-stt/build (only CMake cache remains); rebuild fails: whisper.cpp CMP0002 target_link_libraries error even with GGML_OPENMP=OFF. The live parakeet server on :8796 also references that missing path.
2. ears-server ships kyutai engine only ("SetEngine: engine parakeet-rs not available"); works with default kyutai.
3. With kyutai + current main: session starts, STT partials/final/commit/brain_request_start all fire, but immediately after brain_request_start a turn_interrupted + brain_abort loop begins and no assistant delta ever arrives (see /tmp/traces-base + ~/.local/state/foxline/traces/rust-gateway/52dcdaae*.jsonl, 90 rows). Suspicion: in-flight fxl-n3h5.1 Speech { active } boundary-VAD semantics re-triggering user turns on the fixture's tail audio, or the fixture not modeling eaRS's Speech{active} messages.

Next steps: fix or route around (1) [rebuild worker or use ears], decide (3) by testing the same fixture against the pre-eaRS STT path or gating boundary-VAD, then run baseline-vs-cascade and compare first-audio from traces.
close_reason: Resolved. Root causes fixed/documented: (1) turn_interrupted loop = post-commit decoder-flush partials + boundary-VAD chatter treated as barge-in — fixed in TurnManager with configurable [turn] commit_grace_ms (default 500ms); tests pass. (2) parakeet worker missing -> used ears-server kyutai instead (build fix still open for parakeet path). (3) fixture needed stop-after-tail + absolute workspace + --key=value args. E2E harness works: spqx question wav -> gateway -> eaRS STT -> pi brain (mac-gemma) -> spqx TTS -> audio out. Measured n=7 each: first-audio baseline 5219ms vs cascade 6545ms (drafter steer costs ~1.3s pre-TTS; value requires phase-2 speculative TTS). Full numbers in voice-cascade README.

title: Spike: voice-cascade pi extension (drafter steer + ask_orchestrator tool)
description:
Spike the "channels" idea for voice mode as a pi extension (no gateway changes; Pi stays the only Brain path per ADR-0001). Parent epic: fxl-xwd9.

Cascade tiers (all local, measured warm on this Mac):
- drafter: smollm2:135m via Ollama :11434 — TTFT ~59ms, ~367 tok/s
- speech (main brain): gemma-4-26B-A4B-it Q4_K_M via llama-server :8001, thinking disabled via chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking":false} — content TTFT ~169ms
- orchestrator: deepseek-v4-flash via ds4-serve :8000 — TTFT ~3.7s, ~35 tok/s (prefill-bound)

Phase 1 (this spike): `pi-config/extensions/voice-cascade`:
- `input` hook drafts an opening sentence with the drafter and transforms the prompt so gemma continues from it seamlessly.
- `ask_orchestrator(question)` tool escalates hard queries to ds4 v4 flash.

Phase 2 (later): stream drafter audio to TTS immediately while gemma regenerates (needs Brain trait seam fxl-ma47.2 or gateway-level speculative TTS), adaptive cascade on context length, channel concept for other interaction modes.

Acceptance: extension loads in pi; drafter transform observable in a headless run against mac-gemma provider; orchestrator tool returns ds4 answer; no regression to existing loadouts when disabled.

- Interrupts cancel TTS and abort the Pi Brain.
- Add tests that exercise the orchestration without requiring real Pi/STT/TTS services.
- Preserve the legacy TypeScript bridge path.
- Run cargo check/test and relevant bun checks.

title: In-process streaming parakeet STT via FFI
description:
In-process STT with multiple selectable backends behind SttAdapter:
1. parakeet.cpp TDT 0.6b-v3 (FFI, current) — offline/finalize-only, ~1.9GB RSS, best WER, multilingual (25 EU langs)
2. eaRS Nemotron streaming (parakeet-rs) — true cache-aware streaming partials, ~2.6-2.7GB RSS, WER 0.015, multilingual w/ auto-detect. Quality confirmed good enough by user 2026-07-10.

TDT cannot cache-stream (parakeet.cpp streaming session is RNN-T-only: assert joint_.num_durations() == 0). Nemotron is the only path to true streaming partials today.

Related: fxl-yftd.7 (PiBot checkout dep), fxl-yftd.11 (streaming model eval), fxl-3jey (Silero VAD as reusable eaRS input-stage module).

Results (M-series, 0.6B Base 6bit, mira-chen clone, 24kHz): python-mlx ttfa ~105ms rtf ~0.23 load 8.7s; rust-mlx ttfa ~165ms rtf ~0.28 load 0.6s. WAVs in benchmarks/tts-ab/ for quality judgement.

REMAINING for gateway adoption: (1) worker-command config in ws.rs build_tts_adapter to launch a native binary instead of uv-run-python; (2) ship metallib next to binary in packaging; (3) mirror pop fixes into python worker or retire it (fxl-r8qn.7). spqx repo: 12 commits, mlx-c fork at byteowlz/mlx-c (spqx branch).

Engine: TTFA 96ms median vs python 120, RTF 0.20 vs 0.22, quality validated by listening + ASR. Remaining elsewhere: metallib packaging for distribution (fxl-yftd.10), python worker retirement or pop-fix mirror (fxl-r8qn.7).

Blockers today: voice cloning is x-vector only (no ICL ref-audio+transcript path, likely fails cloning parity gate), no streaming output (TTFA = full generation), reported speedup is vs PyTorch CPU (~3.2 frames/s ≈ RTF>1 on CPU), known F16 autoregressive divergence vs Python. Re-evaluate via benchmarks/tts_ab_bench.py behind a worker shim when it gains ICL cloning + streaming.

title: Python TTS worker: mirror pop fixes or retire it
description: The rust worker's utterance-start pops are fully solved (spqx: warm vocoder state from reference tail, density-based leading-silence click gate, plosive preservation — see spqx-nspf trail). The python worker (services/qwen3_tts_worker.py) still has them, but since all loadouts and the built-in default now use rust-mlx, the python worker is de facto deprecated. DECIDE: (a) mirror the warm-state + gate fixes for parity, or (b) retire it once the rust worker survives real sessions and the binary ships in packaging (fxl-yftd.10) — retirement also closes fxl-yftd.6's filler-port question. Recommendation: keep as A/B reference until the alpha, then retire.

description: Vision pillar 3 (docs/vision.md). Semantic endpointing, event-driven pipeline, streaming-first TTS, real barge-in, CI latency gates. Publish numbers.

title: Cold first-turn latency: brain prewarm does not warm the model
description: Headless live session measured 10.2s from first text_utterance to first audio on a cold session; warm TTS is 96ms — the cost is brain-side (LM Studio 26B model load + system-prompt prefill on first request). lifecycle.prewarm=true only spawns the Pi process. DESIGN (2026-07-08, avoids session pollution): at prewarm, additionally spawn an EPHEMERAL warmup: 'pi --print --no-session' with the IDENTICAL PiLaunch args (same model + append-system-prompt chain) and a trivial one-word prompt, discard output. Effects: provider loads the model (dominant cost) AND prefills the exact same prompt prefix, so LM Studio's prefix/KV cache can serve the real first turn; --no-session writes nothing, the real named session (--continue) sees no fake exchange, history stays clean. Guardrails: loadout flag lifecycle.warmup_prompt (default true), fire-and-forget (never delay session_started), skip when BrainPool returns an already-warm brain. Validate by re-running the headless smoke test and comparing first-turn TTFA cold vs warmed; also record turn-2 TTFA to separate per-session from per-turn cost.
close_reason: Landed: ephemeral pi --print --no-session warmup on prewarm (brain.rs PiLaunch::warmup_launch + spawn_model_warmup; lifecycle.warmup_prompt flag, default true). Validated headless: cold-model baseline 10,170ms first-utterance->first-audio; with warmup 805ms (brain first delta 475ms). Session-history pollution check clean — no new session files. Warmup confirmed loading the 18GB model into LM Studio.

title: Forward Codec interrupt to Pi RPC Brain
close_reason: Done: centralized Rust gateway interrupt handling so explicit Codec interrupt controls and runtime TurnFrame::Interrupted paths abort the active Pi RPC Brain and cancel TTS before resetting frontend audio/phase state. Root cause: only ClientControl::Interrupt directly called brain.abort, while internally generated interrupts went through the runtime frame path and only fanned out TTS cancel frames. Proof: cargo check -p foxline-voice-gateway, cargo test -p foxline-voice-gateway, bun run typecheck, and git diff --check pass.
